question: Which word best completes the analogy: Joy is to presence as sorrow is to — ?
solution:
The correct answer is: **Option (2) i.e. Absence**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **“presence”** refers to the state of being present or existing in a place or situation. (उपस्थिति)

 
 
• **Example:** Her presence at the event was reassuring.
 
 
 
• **“Absence”** is the state of being away or not present; it is the direct opposite of presence. (अनुपस्थिति)
 
 
• **Example:** The absence of his friend made the party less enjoyable.
 
 
 
• In the analogy, as joy relates to presence (something felt when something is present), sorrow relates to absence (something felt when something or someone is missing).

Therefore, the correct answer is- Absence

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Vanishment** (लुप्त होना): The act of disappearing completely.

 
 
• **Example:** The magician’s vanishment amazed the audience.
 
 
 
• **Release** (मुक्ति): The act of setting someone or something free.
 
 
• **Example:** The prisoner’s release brought joy to his family.
 
 
 
• **Quietude** (शांति): A state of stillness, calmness, and quiet in a place.
